brief: ZeroHedge initiates coverage on Tether, framing it as a $191bn balance sheet (Sep 30) that is 64% US T-bills, plus a fast-growing gold hoard, funded by carry income on those reserves. TBAC's 2025 framework projected ~$900bn of incremental stablecoin bill demand by 2028; at Tether's historical 79% issuer share, that implies ~$790bn of Tether bills, and Wednesday's Treasury refunding may shift issuance toward bills, raising the stakes. Jefferies and SocGen separately rank Tether among the largest gold buyers globally (SocGen: 33rd among sovereigns, ~146.5-161t), though Tether's own Q3 attestation shows USDT-backing gold roughly flat, so any Q3 growth likely ran through XAUT or undisclosed corporate holdings, not disclosed reserves. The thesis has a catch: USDT supply stalled in 2026, 9M operating profit ($4.5bn) trails 2025's ~$10bn, and BDO's attestation shows a smaller $1.66bn financial result that does not reconcile to that figure. ZeroHedge argues the slowdown is cyclical, tied to AI debt crowding out Treasury-debasement concerns, and expects both the bill and gold bids to reaccelerate if the AI bubble deflates and emerging-market dollar demand resumes. The GENIUS Act (effective Jan 18, 2027) locks USDT into bills, excludes gold and bitcoin from compliant reserves, and Tether has launched USAT as a compliant competitor to USDC.
